sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien language history. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: ANU (open, hdl:1885/146760).
sources.tag: read: notes on stress
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative/historical, not a Bunu description. p.11: all Hmong-Mien languages tonal; W. Hmongic tone sandhi runs left-to-right. p.199 (sec. 4.2.1): Hmong-Mien nominal prefixes 'are unstressed, and in some languages they may harmonize with the nouns to which they are attached' (family-level remark; Meizhu Bunu prefixed nouns ku1-tau3 'tail', fa3-ɣe1 'stone', pi3-ntsau6 'nose' cited p.201). p.187: Bunu assigns its restricted sandhi tones to Chinese/Zhuang loans. No statement of where word stress falls in Bunu.

sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with restricted access (login, paywall or limited view)
sources.note: Tone-specific first-hand article on the origin of the four extra tone categories 1'–4' of Bunu: per title and per Ratliff 2010:187 (citing Mao & Chou 1972 and Meng 1983) Bunu 'assigns sandhi tones to Chinese and Zhuang borrowings, tones which are restricted in use in the native portion of the vocabulary', and the same minor tones mark 'special purpose' words such as baby-names; i.e. it derives tones 1'–4' from tone-sandhi values and loan strata and describes their spread — implies the 8+4 tone-value system (12 surface values) of Dongnu Bunu. Exact tone values/TBU statements not seen.
